tasks.title: Fix destructive prefix handling, verify bindist hashes, and seal the install environment
tasks.prompt:
You are fixing findings from an adversarial security review of milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

Do not create or edit any other file. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes-triage.md for the full
rationale behind every item below; it records evidence you should not have to re-derive.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (from the M1 brief addendum; obey it):
every file your verify_commands or prompt reads must be (a) inside your own owned_paths,
(b) produced by a task in your depends_on closure, or (c) already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a BUILD ARTIFACT, not committed -- any verify command that needs it must run
`./scripts/build-site.sh` first (committed, idempotent, ~3s warm). The GHC wasm toolchain is
already installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm (GHC 9.14.1.20260731); do not reinstall unless told to.

BACKGROUND
This script installs the pinned GHC WebAssembly toolchain by cloning the GitHub mirror of
ghc-wasm-meta at commit c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455 and running its setup.sh with
FLAVOUR=9.14 and PREFIX=$HOME/.ghc-wasm. Five findings target this file.

=== B1 (BLOCKER): the prefix override can recursively delete arbitrary user data ===
Upstream setup.sh begins with `rm -rf "$PREFIX"`. Your script accepts GHC_WASM_PREFIX without
constraining it, and the "already installed, skip" early-exit does not fire for a directory
that is not a toolchain, so `GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$HOME" ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh` (no
--force!) reaches setup.sh and would delete the user's home directory. This was reproduced.
Fix:
  1. Canonicalise: PREFIX="$(realpath -m "$PREFIX")". Reject any input containing '..'.
  2. HARD-REFUSE list, checked BEFORE anything else and with NO --force override:
       - empty, or "/"
       - exactly "$HOME"
       - the repository root, or any path inside it
       - any ancestor of "$HOME" or of the repository root (e.g. /home, /home/user/..)
     Exit non-zero with a message naming the offending path and why.
  3. If PREFIX exists and is non-empty, it must look like one of OUR toolchain installs before
     any destructive step: accept only if it contains .sxc1-toolchain-stamp, OR contains both
     an `env` file and a `wasm32-wasi-ghc/` directory. Otherwise refuse with a message telling
     the user to pick an empty/new directory. There is NO --force override for this either:
     --force means "reinstall over an existing toolchain", never "wipe arbitrary data".
  4. ALL of the above must run BEFORE the `git clone`, so a refusal touches no network. This is
     what makes the guard cheaply testable; the verify commands depend on it.
  DO NOT implement the "staging directory + rename" idea. It is unsafe here: $PREFIX/env
  contains 21 hard-coded absolute paths (export PATH=/home/.../.ghc-wasm/...), so a rename
  would leave every one of them dangling. Leave a comment saying so, so nobody re-adds it.

=== M1 (MAJOR): none of the ~785 MB of downloads are hash-verified ===
The pinned autogen.json carries SRI digests for every component this host uses
(wasm32-wasi-ghc-9.14, wasi-sdk, libffi-wasm, nodejs, binaryen, wasmtime, cabal -- a mix of
`sha256-<base64>` and `sha512-<base64>`), but setup.sh reads only each `.url`, curls it, and
immediately extracts or `configure && make install`s it.
Fix -- intercept downloads with a curl shim, do NOT patch upstream source:
  1. All seven downloads in the pinned setup.sh use `curl ... -o <file>` (lines 112, 115, 121,
     131, 135, 213, 228). Create a temp shim directory containing an executable `curl` and
     prepend it to PATH **only** for the setup.sh invocation.
  2. The shim must resolve the real curl by ABSOLUTE PATH captured before PATH is modified
     (never by PATH lookup -- that would recurse into itself).
  3. It forwards all arguments to the real curl. On success it parses its own argv for `-o
     <file>` and the http(s) URL, then looks the URL up in the pinned clone's autogen.json:
       jq -r --arg u "$URL" 'to_entries[]|select(.value.url==$u)|.value.hash' autogen.json
  4. Convert the SRI value: strip the `sha256-`/`sha512-` prefix, base64-decode to hex
     (`base64 -d | xxd -p -c256` or openssl), compute the file's digest with the matching
     sha256sum/sha512sum, compare case-insensitively. On mismatch: print the URL, expected and
     actual digests, and EXIT NON-ZERO so setup.sh's `set -e` aborts the install.
  5. FAIL CLOSED: if a download used `-o` and its URL is NOT found in autogen.json, abort.
     (With the M2 fix applied there are no other `-o` downloads; npm's own fetches do not go
     through curl and are integrity-checked by package-lock.json.)
  6. Log one line per verified download and count them. Write the count into the stamp file as
     `sri_verified_downloads=<N>` so a later reviewer can prove a real install went through the
     verifier. On a full install N must be 7.
  7. Add a `--verify-sri-selftest` mode (document it in --help) that exercises the digest
     comparator on a temp file against a known-correct and a known-wrong digest, for BOTH
     sha256 and sha512, and exits non-zero if either behaves wrongly. This makes the security
     control regression-testable in one second instead of one reinstall.

=== M2 (MAJOR): inherited environment variables bypass the pinned sources ===
The pinned setup.sh honours UPSTREAM_WASI_SDK_PIPELINE_ID, UPSTREAM_GHC_PIPELINE_ID,
UPSTREAM_GHC_PROJECT_ID, UPSTREAM_GHC_JOB_NAME, SKIP_GHC, PLAYWRIGHT and NIX_SYSTEM. An ambient
UPSTREAM_GHC_* redirects the compiler download to a caller-chosen GitLab pipeline artifact --
unpinned and unhashed -- and SKIP_GHC=1 wipes the prefix then installs no compiler.
Fix: invoke setup.sh through `env -u` for every one of those variables, e.g.
    env -u UPSTREAM_WASI_SDK_PIPELINE_ID -u UPSTREAM_GHC_PIPELINE_ID -u UPSTREAM_GHC_PROJECT_ID \
        -u UPSTREAM_GHC_JOB_NAME -u SKIP_GHC -u PLAYWRIGHT -u NIX_SYSTEM \
        FLAVOUR="$FLAVOUR" PREFIX="$PREFIX" PATH="$shim:$PATH" bash "$clone/setup.sh"
List them in a commented constant so the list can be re-checked against future pins.

=== M3 (MAJOR, this file's half): health check accepts a stale toolchain ===
check_installed() accepts any readable env plus any wasm32-wasi-ghc that prints a version. It
prints the stamp but never compares it, so after a pin change a restored old toolchain reads as
healthy and the installer exits 0 without installing the new pin.
Fix: make health STRICT. A toolchain is healthy only if ALL hold:
  - the stamp file exists and parses as key=value lines
  - stamp ghc_wasm_meta_commit == the pinned GHC_WASM_META_COMMIT constant
  - stamp flavour == the pinned FLAVOUR constant
  - live `wasm32-wasi-ghc --numeric-version` == stamp ghc_version
  - `wasm32-wasi-cabal --version` succeeds
Any mismatch, or a missing/garbled stamp, is UNHEALTHY -> a normal run reinstalls, and --check
exits non-zero naming the specific mismatch. This is what lets CI self-heal a stale cache.

=== m4 (MINOR): --check fails for irrelevant install prerequisites ===
--check currently runs the full install preflight, so removing unzip or filling the disk makes
a perfectly healthy install report unhealthy -- contradicting its own help text and making it
useless as a post-cache-restore validator.
Fix: split into preflight_install() (git curl tar xz unzip unzstd jq make cc sed realpath +
the 12 GiB free-space check; run only on a real install) and the runtime health check above.
--check runs ONLY the health check. Update --help accordingly.

=== n2 (NIT): de-obfuscate the hostname ===
Line ~7 spells the host `gitlab#dot#haskell#dot#org`. That was unnecessary -- the manifest's
negative greps never matched that prose line either way (verified). Spell it normally:
`gitlab.haskell.org`. Keep describing the upstream `curl ... | sh` install in PROSE rather than
as a literal command line, and keep the explanation of why it is not used.

CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve every existing behaviour not listed above: --help/--check/--force, the pinned
  constants, the rev-parse assertion against the pinned commit, the stamp file's existing keys,
  the final "next steps" output, and `set -euo pipefail`.
- Never pipe a download into a shell.
- Keep the script POSIX-ish bash, no new runtime dependencies beyond coreutils/jq/openssl-or-
  xxd which are already required.

VERIFICATION YOU MUST PERFORM
1. The fast checks in verify_commands below (all network-free).
2. ONE full reinstall to prove the curl shim does not break the real install:
     ./scripts/install-toolchain.sh --force
   This takes 15-40 minutes and downloads ~785 MB -- run it as a BACKGROUND job with output
   teed to a log and poll it; it will exceed a 10-minute foreground command timeout. Afterwards
   confirm the stamp records `sri_verified_downloads=7` and that build-site.sh still works
   (`./scripts/build-site.sh && ./scripts/check-site.sh`). Report the count and the timing.
3. Prove the SRI verifier actually rejects bad data: describe in your report how you confirmed
   a corrupted download aborts the install (the --verify-sri-selftest path is the cheap way).
verify_commands: bash -n /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh && test -x /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh

bash -c 'set -e
W=$(mktemp -d)
cat > "$W/git" <<"EOS"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
if [ "$1" = "clone" ]; then
  mkdir -p "$3"
  printf "#!/usr/bin/env bash\necho \"SETUP_REACHED_PREFIX=\$PREFIX\"\n" > "$3/setup.sh"
  chmod +x "$3/setup.sh"
fi
if [ "$1" = "-C" ] && [ "$3" = "rev-parse" ]; then
  echo c75985a1b58fb0376eea9149ba5c7b933b3c7455
fi
exit 0
EOS
chmod +x "$W/git"
V=$(mktemp -d); echo precious > "$V/data.txt"
rc=0
for p in "$HOME" / /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 /home "$V"; do
  out=$(PATH="$W:$PATH" GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$p" timeout 30 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh 2>&1 || true)
  if printf "%s" "$out" | grep -q SETUP_REACHED_PREFIX; then
    echo "FAIL: control reached upstream setup.sh with PREFIX=$p (would rm -rf it)"; rc=1
  fi
done
test -f "$V/data.txt" || { echo "FAIL: victim data destroyed"; rc=1; }
rm -rf "$W" "$V"
test $rc -eq 0 && echo "ok: no unsafe prefix reaches setup.sh"
exit $rc'

bash -c 'set -e; D=$(mktemp -d); out=$(GHC_WASM_PREFIX="$D/x" timeout 20 /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check 2>&1 || true); case "$out" in *clon*|*Clon*) echo "FAIL: --check appears to hit the network"; exit 1;; esac; rm -rf "$D"; echo "ok: --check performs no clone"'
/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --verify-sri-selftest

bash -c 'set -e; S="$HOME/.ghc-wasm/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"; B=$(mktemp); cp "$S" "$B"; trap "cp \"$B\" \"$S\"; rm -f \"$B\"" EXIT; sed -i "s/^ghc_wasm_meta_commit=.*/ghc_wasm_meta_commit=deadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeefdeadbeef/" "$S"; if /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "FAIL: --check accepted a mismatched pin"; exit 1; fi; echo "ok: stamp pin mismatch detected"'

bash -c 'set -e; D=$(mktemp -d); for f in /usr/bin/* /bin/*; do b=$(basename "$f"); case "$b" in unzip|unzstd|make|cc|gcc) continue;; esac; ln -sf "$f" "$D/$b" 2>/dev/null || true; done; PATH="$D" "$D/bash" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL: --check needs install-only prerequisites"; exit 1; }; rm -rf "$D"; echo "ok: --check is a pure health probe"'
/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh --check
grep -q 'sri_verified_downloads=' "$HOME/.ghc-wasm/.sxc1-toolchain-stamp"

bash -c 'for v in UPSTREAM_WASI_SDK_PIPELINE_ID UPSTREAM_GHC_PIPELINE_ID UPSTREAM_GHC_PROJECT_ID UPSTREAM_GHC_JOB_NAME SKIP_GHC PLAYWRIGHT NIX_SYSTEM; do grep -q "$v" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh || { echo "FAIL: $v not neutralised"; exit 1; }; done; echo "ok: upstream control variables handled"'
bash -c 'grep -q "gitlab\.haskell\.org" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh && ! grep -q "#dot#" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh'
bash -c '! grep -nE "^[^#]*curl[^|]*\|[[:space:]]*(sh|bash)" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/install-toolchain.sh'
acceptance_checks: B1: the prefix guard runs before any git clone and refuses /, $HOME, the repo root, ancestors of either, paths containing '..', and any existing non-toolchain directory; --force does not override any of these; a populated victim directory survives an attempted install.
B1: no staging-directory/rename scheme was introduced, and a comment records why (env bakes 21 absolute paths).

M1: every setup.sh download is intercepted by a PATH-prepended curl shim that resolves the real curl by absolute path, verifies the autogen.json SRI digest (sha256 and sha512 both supported), aborts non-zero on mismatch, and fails closed on any -o download absent from autogen.json.

M1: --verify-sri-selftest exercises both digest algorithms against known-good and known-bad values and exits non-zero if either misbehaves; a real --force reinstall completed and recorded sri_verified_downloads=7 in the stamp.
M2: setup.sh is invoked with UPSTREAM_WASI_SDK_PIPELINE_ID, UPSTREAM_GHC_PIPELINE_ID, UPSTREAM_GHC_PROJECT_ID, UPSTREAM_GHC_JOB_NAME, SKIP_GHC, PLAYWRIGHT and NIX_SYSTEM explicitly unset.

M3: health requires an exact stamp match on pinned commit and flavour plus a live GHC version equal to the recorded one and a working wasm32-wasi-cabal; a mutated stamp makes --check fail and a normal run reinstall.
m4: --check runs only the runtime health probe -- it succeeds on a healthy install with unzip/unzstd/make/cc absent from PATH, and performs no network access.
n2: the hostname is spelled gitlab.haskell.org normally, the upstream install is still described in prose rather than as a literal pipeline, and no test-evasion obfuscation remains.
All pre-existing behaviour is preserved: --help/--check/--force, pinned constants, rev-parse assertion, stamp keys, and set -euo pipefail.

tasks.title: Bound every CDP wait by the deadline and stop reporting missing DOM nodes as success
tasks.prompt:
You are fixing findings from an adversarial security review of milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs

Do not create or edit any other file. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes-triage.md for full rationale.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (from the M1 brief addendum; obey it):
every file your verify_commands or prompt reads must be (a) inside your own owned_paths,
(b) produced by a task in your depends_on closure, or (c) already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a BUILD ARTIFACT, not committed -- any verify command that needs it must run
`./scripts/build-site.sh` first (committed, idempotent, ~3s warm). The GHC wasm toolchain is
already installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm (GHC 9.14.1.20260731); do not reinstall unless told to.

BACKGROUND
browser-check.mjs launches headless Google Chrome, drives it over the DevTools Protocol using
only Node built-ins (global WebSocket -- no npm packages, ever), and asserts the WASM/Miso
counter app boots and works. Two findings target it.

=== M4 (MAJOR): the advertised --timeout does not bound connection or protocol commands ===
Today CDPClient.send() stores {resolve, reject} in this.pending with NO timer; the only
resolver is _onMessage; nothing rejects pending calls when the socket closes or errors; and
connectWebSocket resolves on 'open'/rejects on 'error' with NO deadline, so a peer that accepts
TCP but never completes the WebSocket handshake hangs forever. --timeout is consulted only by
the polling loops. Combined with check-site.sh having no outer bound, a 45-second harness can
hang until CI's multi-hour job limit.
Fix:
  1. Establish ONE monotonic deadline at startup: deadlineAt = Date.now() + timeoutMs. Add a
     helper `remaining()` and a `withDeadline(promise, label)` that rejects with a clear
     "<label> exceeded the --timeout budget" error when the remaining budget runs out.
  2. Route EVERY await through it: connectWebSocket, each CDPClient.send, each polling loop.
  3. CDPClient.send: also attach a per-command timer so a silently dropped command rejects
     rather than leaking a pending entry; clear it whenever the promise settles.
  4. Register ws 'close' and 'error' listeners that reject and CLEAR every pending call with a
     descriptive error, so an in-flight command cannot outlive the socket.
  5. Wire the browser child process: on 'exit' or 'error' during the run, reject all pending
     calls and fail the run with the exit code/signal.
  6. Every one of these paths must still run the existing cleanup (kill the process group,
     remove the temp profile) exactly once.
  Exit codes stay: 0 all assertions passed, 1 an assertion failed, 2 harness error
  (no browser, CDP unreachable, deadline exceeded).

=== m3 (MINOR): missing DOM nodes are handled inconsistently, one assertion is vacuous ===
Two distinct bugs:
  (a) A missing #btn-increment/#btn-decrement/#btn-reset makes `querySelector(...).click()`
      throw, which escapes the assertion block and is reported as exit 2 "harness error"
      instead of a plain assertion failure (exit 1).
  (b) Worse, the boot-status assertion is:
          const e = document.querySelector('#boot-status');
          if (!e) return true;          // <-- absence reported as SUCCESS
      Deleting #boot-status from the page makes "ok - #boot-status is hidden after boot" PASS.
      This was reproduced: a page with no #boot-status scored a full 17/17 through check-site.
      The shared boot contract REQUIRES #boot-status -- without it a boot failure has nowhere
      to render.
Fix:
  1. Add an `assertElement(selector)` helper that evaluates
     `document.querySelector(sel) !== null` and reports absence as an ordinary FAILED assertion
     with a clear message, never as a throw and never as a pass.
  2. Use it before every click, and make each click a reported assertion rather than a bare
     evaluate that can throw through the block.
  3. Replace the boot-status check with TWO conditions in one assertion: the element must
     EXIST and must be hidden (`e.hidden === true || e.offsetParent === null`). Absence fails.
  4. Keep the existing assertion names and the "N/M assertions passed" summary format --
     check-site.sh and CI parse them.

CONSTRAINTS
- Zero npm dependencies. No package.json, no node_modules, Node built-ins only.
- Preserve --url, --browser, --timeout, --self-test, --keep-open and the SXC1_BROWSER env var.
- --self-test must still pass and must exercise the same code path as a real run.
- Keep the process-group kill + retrying temp-profile removal that a previous agent added; it
  fixed a real Chrome helper-process leak.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
`node scripts/browser-check.mjs --self-test` passes; a page that never boots fails within the
--timeout budget instead of hanging; a page missing a button fails with exit 1 (not 2); and a
page missing #boot-status FAILS. The verify commands below build the real site first (with the
committed ./scripts/build-site.sh) and sabotage copies of it under /tmp -- never modify
site/public in place.
verify_commands: node --check /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs && test -x /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs

bash -c '! grep -nE "require\\(.(puppeteer|playwright|ws|jsdom)|from .(puppeteer|playwright|ws|jsdom)" /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs' && test ! -e /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/package.json && test ! -e /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/node_modules
node /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs --self-test

bash -c 'set -e; D=$(mktemp -d); printf "<!doctype html><title>x</title><body>never boots</body>" > "$D/index.html"; P=8791; (cd "$D" && nohup python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 $P >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > "$D/pid"); sleep 1; s=$(date +%s); set +e; timeout 60 node /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:$P/ --timeout 8000 >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e; e=$(( $(date +%s) - s )); kill $(cat "$D/pid") 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$D"; test $rc -ne 0 || { echo "FAIL: non-booting page reported success"; exit 1; }; test $rc -ne 124 || { echo "FAIL: harness hung past its own deadline"; exit 1; }; test $e -lt 45 || { echo "FAIL: took ${e}s, deadline not enforced"; exit 1; }; echo "ok: deadline enforced (rc=$rc, ${e}s)"'

bash -c 'set -e; cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 && ./scripts/build-site.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; D=$(mktemp -d); cp -R site/public/. "$D/"; python3 -c "import re,sys; p=sys.argv[1]; s=open(p).read(); s2=re.sub(r\"
\", \"\", s, flags=re.S); assert s2!=s; open(p,\"w\").write(s2)" "$D/index.html"; P=8792; (cd "$D" && nohup python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 $P >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/bc2.pid); sleep 1; set +e; timeout 90 node /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:$P/ >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e; kill $(cat /tmp/bc2.pid) 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$D" /tmp/bc2.pid; test $rc -eq 1 || { echo "FAIL: missing #boot-status gave rc=$rc, expected 1"; exit 1; }; echo "ok: missing #boot-status is a failed assertion"'

bash -c 'set -e; cd /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1 && ./scripts/build-site.sh >/dev/null 2>&1; D=$(mktemp -d); cp -R site/public/. "$D/"; printf "<script>new MutationObserver(function(){var b=document.getElementById(\"btn-increment\"); if(b) b.remove();}).observe(document.documentElement,{childList:true,subtree:true});</script>" >> "$D/index.html"; P=8793; (cd "$D" && nohup python3 -m http.server --bind 127.0.0.1 $P >/dev/null 2>&1 & echo $! > /tmp/bc3.pid); sleep 1; set +e; timeout 90 node /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/browser-check.mjs --url http://127.0.0.1:$P/ >/dev/null 2>&1; rc=$?; set -e; kill $(cat /tmp/bc3.pid) 2>/dev/null || true; rm -rf "$D" /tmp/bc3.pid; test $rc -eq 1 || { echo "FAIL: missing #btn-increment gave rc=$rc, expected 1 (assertion failure, not 2)"; exit 1; }; echo "ok: missing button is a failed assertion, not a harness error"'
acceptance_checks: M4: a single monotonic deadline bounds the WebSocket connect, every CDP command and every polling loop; a page that never boots fails within the --timeout budget rather than hanging (measured).
M4: ws 'close'/'error' and browser child 'exit'/'error' reject and clear all pending CDP calls; cleanup (process-group kill + temp profile removal) still runs exactly once on every exit path.
M4: CDPClient.send attaches and clears a per-command timer so dropped commands cannot leak pending entries.
m3: a missing required element is reported as an ordinary failed assertion with exit 1, not as an exit-2 harness error.
m3: the #boot-status assertion requires the element to EXIST and be hidden; deleting it from the page now FAILS (previously a vacuous pass that scored 17/17).
Exit-code contract holds: 0 all passed, 1 assertion failed, 2 harness error (no browser / CDP unreachable / deadline exceeded).
Still zero npm dependencies; --self-test passes and exercises the same code path as a real run; existing assertion names and the 'N/M assertions passed' summary format are unchanged.

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/scripts/check-site.sh

Do not create or edit any other file. scripts/browser-check.mjs is being fixed in parallel by
the task you depend on -- call it, do not edit it. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes-triage.md first.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (from the M1 brief addendum; obey it):
every file your verify_commands or prompt reads must be (a) inside your own owned_paths,
(b) produced by a task in your depends_on closure, or (c) already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a BUILD ARTIFACT, not committed -- any verify command that needs it must run
`./scripts/build-site.sh` first (committed, idempotent, ~3s warm). The GHC wasm toolchain is
already installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm (GHC 9.14.1.20260731); do not reinstall unless told to.

BACKGROUND
check-site.sh is the single command that proves M0's definition of done. Five findings target
it, and TWO of them are vacuous-success paths: the script currently reports "17/17 checks
passed" on bundles that are provably broken.

=== M9 (MAJOR, worst finding): the Pages-subpath invariant is not actually tested ===
The root-absolute-URL scan recognises only four double-quoted spellings. Changing
`fetch("./app.wasm")` to the equally valid `fetch('/app.wasm')` is NOT detected, and because
the browser test serves at http://127.0.0.1:<port>/ where /app.wasm resolves fine, the whole
run passes. Reproduced: the sabotaged bundle scored 17/17 here, yet served under a project
sub-path it scored 0/7 assertions -- totally dead. The real bundle scores 6/6 at the same
sub-path, so a sub-path run cleanly discriminates.
Fix -- make it a BEHAVIOURAL test, which is what the property actually is:
  1. Serve the bundle under a NON-ROOT prefix and run the browser check there. Concretely:
     create a temp dir, copy the bundle to "<tmp>/sub/path/", serve <tmp> and point

  2. Keep a root-served browser run too (it is the ordinary smoke test).

     cover single AND double quotes, template literals, CSS url(/...), new URL('/...', ...),

     authoritative and the grep is advisory -- so nobody "fixes" a future miss by widening the
     regex alone.
  4. Report the sub-path run as its own named check.

=== M5 (MAJOR): Node is required but never resolved or documented ===
check-site.sh calls bare `node` (for the wasm export check and to run browser-check.mjs) and
never sources the toolchain env. A host meeting every documented prerequisite can have no
system node; install-toolchain.sh does install a private Node under $HOME/.ghc-wasm but nothing
exports it. A too-old Node without global WebSocket also fails late and confusingly.
Fix: resolve Node explicitly, in this order:
     $SXC1_NODE  >  "$GHC_WASM_PREFIX"/nodejs/bin/node (default prefix $HOME/.ghc-wasm)  >  `node` on PATH
  Validate the chosen binary once: it must run and report `typeof WebSocket === "function"` and
  have WebAssembly. If none qualifies, FAIL with an actionable message naming SXC1_NODE, the
  minimum version (Node 22+ for global WebSocket; 24 is what M0 was validated on) and the
  toolchain's private Node path. Use the resolved binary everywhere -- both the export check
  and the browser-check.mjs invocation. Print which Node was chosen and its version.

=== m1 (MINOR): port TOCTOU / can validate an unrelated server ===
port_in_use() probes and releases, and wait_for_port() proves only that SOMEBODY is listening.
Fix: after starting the server, (a) confirm the server child is still alive, and (b) fetch
/index.html from the chosen port and require it to byte-match the on-disk file (compare
checksums) before launching the browser. Fail with a clear message if it does not. Apply the
same guard to the sub-path server from M9.

=== m2 (MINOR): skipping the browser axis still reports a complete success ===
--skip-browser / SXC1_SKIP_BROWSER=1 exits 0 printing "check-site: 16/16 checks passed",
indistinguishable from a full gate to anything recording only status or the fraction.

"check-site: 16/17 checks passed (1 skipped)". Emit a machine-readable final marker line:
  `check-site: result=complete`          when every axis ran
  `check-site: result=structural-only`   when the browser axis was skipped
Exit 0 is still fine for the explicit local escape hatch. CI will assert result=complete.

=== n1 (NIT): SERVER_LOG leaks one temp file per run ===
SERVER_LOG is created for every browser run but cleanup only kills SERVER_PID. 16 files
accumulated during one review session.
Fix: track every server log in cleanup; delete on success; on failure print its contents (more
useful than leaving it on disk) and then delete it. Handle both servers from M9.

tasks.prompt:
You are fixing findings from an adversarial security review of milestone M0 of the
SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly ONE file:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/.github/workflows/site.yml

Do not create or edit any other file -- call the scripts, do not modify them. Read
/home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes-triage.md for rationale.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (from the M1 brief addendum; obey it):
every file your verify_commands or prompt reads must be (a) inside your own owned_paths,
(b) produced by a task in your depends_on closure, or (c) already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a BUILD ARTIFACT, not committed -- any verify command that needs it must run
`./scripts/build-site.sh` first (committed, idempotent, ~3s warm). The GHC wasm toolchain is
already installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm (GHC 9.14.1.20260731); do not reinstall unless told to.

The scripts you invoke are fixed by tasks in your depends_on closure, so you may rely on their
new behaviour: `./scripts/install-toolchain.sh` is idempotent and now self-heals a stale
toolchain via a strict stamp check, and `./scripts/check-site.sh` now prints a final marker
line `check-site: result=complete` (or `result=structural-only` if the browser axis was
skipped).

OWNER DEPENDENCY -- READ THIS BEFORE DESIGNING THE DEPLOY GATE
The GitHub repository does not exist yet: its name and visibility are still open questions with
the owner (PLAN.md open question 1), and GitHub Pages requires a public repo on a free account.
Your gate must therefore be SAFE UNDER EITHER OUTCOME and must need no code change when the
decision lands. Use an explicit repository variable opt-in (below), never an assumption.

=== M6 (MAJOR): the deploy job is not inert while Pages is disabled ===
Its only condition is a non-PR main ref, so the first push to main after the repo is created
runs actions/deploy-pages even if Pages was never configured for Actions -- failing the job and
the whole workflow. The comment and README claim it stays inert; nothing encodes that.
Fix: add `vars.ENABLE_PAGES == 'true'` to the deploy job's `if`. Unset variable (the default)
-> job skipped -> main stays green. When the owner enables Pages they set the repository
variable once. Update the job's comment to describe exactly this, including the variable name.

=== M7 (MAJOR): PR build code receives deployment and OIDC permissions ===
pages:write and id-token:write are declared at WORKFLOW scope, so the build job -- which runs
repository-controlled shell scripts on pull_request -- holds them too.
Fix: workflow-level `permissions: contents: read`. Give the build job `permissions: contents:
read`. Give ONLY the deploy job `pages: write` and `id-token: write` (plus contents: read).
Add `with: persist-credentials: false` to actions/checkout -- no later step needs git auth.

=== M8 (MAJOR): one constant concurrency group can discard a pending main deployment ===
Every push, PR and manual run shares `group: pages` across the whole expensive build. GitHub
keeps only ONE pending run per group and a newly queued run replaces and cancels the existing
pending one -- so a pending main build can be evicted by an unrelated PR and never deploy. PR
checks are also needlessly serialized behind 15-60 minute installs.
Fix: remove the workflow-level concurrency block entirely.
  - build job: `concurrency: { group: build-${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }},
    cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }} }`
    (superseded PRs cancel; main builds are never cancelled mid-flight).
  - deploy job only: `concurrency: { group: pages, cancel-in-progress: false }`.

=== M3 (MAJOR, this file's half): restore-keys silently defeat pin upgrades ===
`restore-keys: ghc-wasm-${{ runner.os }}-` restores an OLD toolchain when the pin changes;
cache-hit is then 'false' so the installer runs, and previously it exited 0 because the stale
compiler "worked" -- and actions/cache then saved that stale tree under the NEW key, poisoning
it. runner.os is only "Linux", so an image migration can restore binaries built for a
materially different image.
Fix:
  1. DELETE the toolchain cache's `restore-keys` entirely. The tree is immutable, not
     incrementally reusable -- a partial match is never desirable.
  2. Key it on runner.os, runner.arch, the runner image (`env.ImageOS`) and
     hashFiles('scripts/install-toolchain.sh').
  3. Run `./scripts/install-toolchain.sh` UNCONDITIONALLY (drop the
     `if: cache-hit != 'true'`). It is idempotent, exits in ~1s when the stamp matches the pin,
     and now reinstalls when it does not -- which is exactly the self-healing behaviour needed
     after a stale restore. Keep timeout-minutes: 60 on that step.
  4. Leave the site/dist-newstyle cache's restore-keys alone: that one IS incrementally
     reusable and a partial match is genuinely useful.

=== M4 (MAJOR, this file's half): no backstop timeout on verification ===
The Verify site step has no timeout-minutes, so a hung harness runs to GitHub's job limit.
Fix: add `timeout-minutes: 15` to the Verify site step and `timeout-minutes: 30` to Build site.

=== m2 (MINOR, this file's half): CI must reject a silently-skipped browser axis ===
Fix: capture check-site.sh's output and fail the step unless it contains
`check-site: result=complete`. Something like:
    ./scripts/check-site.sh | tee /tmp/check-site.log
    grep -q 'check-site: result=complete' /tmp/check-site.log \
      || { echo "::error::browser verification did not run"; exit 1; }
Use `set -o pipefail` (GitHub's default bash shell already sets `-o pipefail`) so a failing
check-site.sh still fails the step.

CONSTRAINTS
- Only first-party actions/* -- no third-party actions. No Nix, ghcup, stack, system GHC, or
  npm/node setup steps.
- Keep: triggers (push to main, pull_request, workflow_dispatch), the build->deploy ordering,
  upload-pages-artifact@v5 with path site/public, deploy-pages@v5, and the failure debug
  artifact upload.
- Every `run:` step must invoke a script that exists; check with `ls` before finishing.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
The file parses as YAML, the structural assertions in the verify commands pass, and you can
explain step by step how a cold runner would proceed. You cannot execute GitHub Actions
locally; in your report, state which local command you ran to confirm each equivalent
behaviour (e.g. that install-toolchain.sh --check is fast and that check-site.sh prints
result=complete).

M0 of the SXC-1 Trainer project. Repository root: /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1. You own exactly these two files:

    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/README.md
    /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-plan.md

Do not create or edit anything else. Read /home/mrcolson/repos/casio-sxc1/briefs/M0-fixes-triage.md first -- it is the
authoritative record of what was found and how each item was fixed in code.

DEPENDENCY-CLOSURE RULE (from the M1 brief addendum; obey it):
every file your verify_commands or prompt reads must be (a) inside your own owned_paths,
(b) produced by a task in your depends_on closure, or (c) already committed at HEAD.
site/public/ is a BUILD ARTIFACT, not committed -- any verify command that needs it must run
`./scripts/build-site.sh` first (committed, idempotent, ~3s warm). The GHC wasm toolchain is
already installed at $HOME/.ghc-wasm (GHC 9.14.1.20260731); do not reinstall unless told to.

Everything you document has already been implemented by the tasks in your depends_on closure.
Read the current scripts/install-toolchain.sh, scripts/check-site.sh and
.github/workflows/site.yml before writing, and describe what they ACTUALLY do -- do not copy
claims from this prompt without checking. Several findings exist precisely because the previous
docs asserted properties the code did not have.

=== M1: the integrity claim is overstated in BOTH files ===
README.md ("Why not the documented one-liner") and briefs/M0-plan.md (section 3 pin table and
section 4.2) currently generalise git's commit verification into a claim that no download
checksums are needed -- e.g. "git verifies the content by commit hash, so there is no separate
checksum file to maintain". That conflates SOURCE integrity with BINDIST integrity: the git
commit authenticates only the ghc-wasm-meta source tree, while ~785 MB of compilers and SDKs
were downloaded with no verification at all, even though the pinned autogen.json contains SRI
digests for every one of them.
Fix in both files: state the distinction plainly, and describe the control that now exists --
install-toolchain.sh routes every setup.sh download through a curl shim that verifies the
autogen.json SRI digest (sha256/sha512), fails closed on any unpinned -o download, and records
`sri_verified_downloads=N` in the toolchain stamp. In briefs/M0-plan.md, update risk R1's
"Residual" sentence, which currently accepts this gap, to say it is now closed and how.

=== B1: the "nothing outside $HOME/.ghc-wasm is touched" claim ===
README.md's prerequisites section says nothing outside $HOME/.ghc-wasm is touched. That was
false for a custom GHC_WASM_PREFIX (upstream setup.sh starts with `rm -rf "$PREFIX"`).
Fix: document GHC_WASM_PREFIX honestly -- what it does, that the installer refuses unsafe
targets (/, $HOME, the repo, ancestors of either, and any existing directory that is not
already a toolchain install), and that --force reinstalls over an existing toolchain but never
wipes arbitrary data.

=== M5: Node is a real prerequisite and is undocumented ===
README's prerequisites list has no mention of Node at all, yet ./scripts/check-site.sh needs it.
Fix: add Node to the prerequisites with a concrete minimum version (Node 22+ is required for
the global WebSocket used by the browser driver; M0 was validated on Node 24), note that the
toolchain installs a private Node under $HOME/.ghc-wasm that check-site.sh will fall back to,
and document the SXC1_NODE override. Add a troubleshooting entry.

=== m5: the file:// claim is false ===
README's "How it works" ends by claiming the bundle works "at any GitHub Pages sub-path, at a
domain root, or offline from a local directory". Opening index.html as file:// cannot work: it
is an ES module that imports sibling modules and fetches app.wasm, and browsers give file://
an opaque origin that blocks both.
Fix: say "offline when served locally (./scripts/serve-site.sh)" and state plainly that
file:// is not supported and why. Do NOT add a packaging mode -- that would be feature creep.

=== M6: document the Pages opt-in ===
The deploy job is now gated on the repository variable ENABLE_PAGES == 'true'.
Fix: in README's Deployment section, explain that CI builds and verifies on every push while
deployment stays inert until the owner (a) makes the repo public, (b) enables Pages with the
GitHub Actions source, and (c) sets the repository variable ENABLE_PAGES to true. Keep the
existing note that this is an open question in PLAN.md.

=== Also document the new verification behaviour ===
README should mention that check-site.sh now serves the bundle under a non-root sub-path and
runs the browser check there (this is what actually enforces GitHub Pages sub-path
compatibility), and that it prints `result=complete` vs `result=structural-only` so CI can tell
a full gate from a structural-only run.

CONSTRAINTS
- Keep both documents' existing structure, tone and section ordering. These are edits, not
  rewrites.
- Do not change any pinned version. If a measured figure changed because of the fixes, re-measure
  rather than guessing: `./scripts/build-site.sh` then `./scripts/check-site.sh` are cheap.
- briefs/M0-plan.md is the design record of the milestone. Correct the specific claims named
  above and R1's residual; do not restructure it or delete the original reasoning -- where a
  claim was wrong, the correction should read as a correction.
- Every command you print in README must be one you have run.

DONE LOOKS LIKE
Both files are accurate about what the code now does, a reader following README on a minimal
Linux host can succeed, and no sentence overstates a security property.
